review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines the product and sum topologies (instances) and a set of Homeomorph defs: prodCongr, prodComm, prodAssoc, prodProdProdComm, prodPUnit, punitProd, sumCongr, sumComm, sumAssoc, sumSumSumComm, sumEmpty, emptySum, sumProdDistrib and prodSumDistrib. A grep over Mathlib shows the same names only for other structures (Equiv, UniformEquiv, MeasurableEquiv, LinearEquiv and so on). Those are the ≃ₜ-level analogues in each category, built on the Equiv versions through `toEquiv`. No other topological-space definition in Mathlib duplicates them. The aliases `Continuous.along_fst`/`along_snd` and the `IsClosed.setOf_mapsTo` deprecation are alias or deprecation patterns, not independent competing definitions. The file has no other new structures or definitions. The remaining duplicate-looking items are theorems (for example the `isInducing_prodMkLeft` and `isEmbedding_prodMkLeft` pairs, and `Continuous.uncurry_left` against `continuous_curry`), which the rubric excludes. I found no justified finding.
